text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds took a swift trip south in late trade as jitters in U.S. credit markets fed through to Germany and sparked what traders described as panic selling. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.80, down 0/57 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts were hit hard in afternoon trade and slid lower with Bunds in very light turnover ahead of 3-day weekend in Germany, U.S. Treasuries were also down after stronger than expected preliminary University of Michigan survey. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-26/32, down 20/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures lost almost all of this week's gains as Bund weakness undermined an otherwise positive start which was helped by an opinion poll giving the French centre-right a majority in a May 25/June 1 election. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.88, down 0.38 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ending the week with net gains overall but on plateau in comparison to last couple of days, with the market digesting significance of German plan to revalue gold reserves in bid to meet EMU criteria. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.17, down 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries continue to work lower after preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment index rises to 104.6 in May, vs 101.4 Apr, April housing starts rose 2.6 pct to 1.473 million units. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-02/32, down 08/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.89 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended the Tokyo session higher on short-covering by dealers ahead of the weekend. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.26, up 0.49 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - New issues business was dominated by a host of banks normally more identifiable as lead managers rather than borrowers. Goldman Sachs launched a $400 million FRN while UBS set a $250 million convertible.
The most conventional deal was Toronto-Dominion Bank's offering of a $250 million five-year deal at a 21 basis points yield spread via IBJ International.
